chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Permitted to you is the grazing livestock' [Quran 5:1], so he said: 'The fetus in its mother's womb, when it grows hair and becomes thick-coated, its slaughter is the same as the slaughter of its mother; that is what Allah, Exalted, meant.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a fetus to be considered halal to eat along with its mother in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the condition of 'ash'ara wa abwara' (hair growth and thickening of the coat) as the marker for a fetus's independent ritual status. It establishes that the fetus is consumed with the mother without separate slaughter, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the fetus inherits the mother’s state of purity and slaughter validity. This ruling is crucial for understanding the practical application of Quranic permissions regarding livestock in Shia fiqh.
